questions.stem: What privilege is required to view the warehouse load monitoring chart in Snowsight?

options.text: USAGE on the warehouse
OPERATE on the warehouse
OWNERSHIP of the warehouse
MONITOR on the warehouse

explanation.correct: To view the load monitoring chart, you must use a role that has the MONITOR privilege on the warehouse.

distractors.A: USAGE allows running queries on the warehouse but does not grant access to the monitoring chart.
distractors.B: OPERATE allows starting/stopping the warehouse but is not the required privilege for viewing load charts.
distractors.C: OWNERSHIP provides full control but is not the minimum required privilege.

questions.stem: What is the maximum time range that the warehouse load monitoring chart can display in Snowsight?

options.text: 7 days
30 days
2 weeks
1 month

explanation.correct: The warehouse load monitoring chart displays data over a two-week (2 weeks) period maximum.

distractors.A: 7 days is less than the maximum range of 2 weeks.

questions.stem: Which SQL command changes the current warehouse for an active session?

options.text: SET WAREHOUSE = my_wh
ALTER SESSION SET DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE = my_wh
USE WAREHOUSE my_wh
SELECT CURRENT_WAREHOUSE(my_wh)

explanation.correct: USE WAREHOUSE changes the current warehouse for the session at any time.

distractors.A: SET WAREHOUSE is not a valid SQL command.
distractors.B: ALTER SESSION does not support a DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE parameter.
distractors.D: CURRENT_WAREHOUSE() returns the name; it cannot set it.

questions.stem: Which THREE privileges are equivalent to the MANAGE WAREHOUSES account-level privilege? (Select THREE)

options.text: USAGE on all warehouses
MODIFY on all warehouses
MONITOR on all warehouses
OPERATE on all warehouses
OWNERSHIP on all warehouses
CREATE WAREHOUSE on account

explanation.correct: MANAGE WAREHOUSES is equivalent to granting MODIFY, MONITOR, and OPERATE privileges on all warehouses in the account.

distractors.A: USAGE allows running queries on a warehouse but is not part of MANAGE WAREHOUSES.
distractors.E: OWNERSHIP grants full control including the ability to drop; it is not included in MANAGE WAREHOUSES.
distractors.F: CREATE WAREHOUSE is a separate account-level privilege for creating new warehouses.

questions.stem: Which TWO operations does a virtual warehouse provide compute resources for? (Select TWO)

options.text: Executing DDL commands like CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE
Loading data into tables using COPY INTO <table>
Executing SELECT statements that require compute resources
Managing user authentication and session tokens
Storing table data in micro-partitions

explanation.correct: Virtual warehouses provide compute resources for executing SQL SELECT statements and DML operations including loading data with COPY INTO <table>.

distractors.A: Most DDL commands are handled by the cloud services layer and do not require a running warehouse.
distractors.D: Authentication and session management are handled by the cloud services layer, not warehouses.
distractors.E: Data storage is handled by the storage layer, not the compute warehouse.

questions.scenario: An administrator notices that warehouse load has been consistently high with queuing during business hours, but nearly zero overnight.
questions.stem: Which TWO actions could address this pattern? (Select TWO)

options.text: Create a separate warehouse and redirect some peak workload to it
Increase the auto-suspend timeout to keep the warehouse warm
Configure multi-cluster settings to add clusters during peak concurrency
Decrease the warehouse size to reduce credit usage
Disable auto-resume to prevent overnight startups

explanation.correct: Moving peak workload to a separate warehouse or configuring multi-cluster to add clusters during high concurrency are both recommended approaches for handling recurring peak loads.

distractors.B: Increasing auto-suspend does not help with peak concurrency; it only affects idle periods.
distractors.D: Decreasing size would worsen the queuing problem during peak hours.
distractors.E: Disabling auto-resume is unrelated to managing peak-hour concurrency.

questions.scenario: A warehouse is currently running queries. An administrator executes ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh SUSPEND.
questions.stem: What happens to the currently executing queries?

options.text: All queries are immediately terminated and the warehouse shuts down
Idle resources shut down immediately; resources executing statements continue until statements complete, then shut down
The suspend command fails because queries are running
All queries are moved to a system queue and resumed when the warehouse restarts

explanation.correct: When you suspend a warehouse, Snowflake immediately shuts down idle compute resources but allows resources executing statements to continue until completion, then shuts them down (quiesce mode).

distractors.A: Running queries are not immediately terminated; they complete before resources shut down.
distractors.C: The suspend command does not fail; it initiates graceful shutdown.
distractors.D: Queries are not moved to a queue; they complete on their current resources.

questions.scenario: A data engineer wants to verify that new compute resources are fully provisioned after resizing their warehouse from Small to Large.
questions.stem: Which parameter should they add to the ALTER WAREHOUSE command?

options.text: VALIDATE_RESOURCES = TRUE
WAIT_FOR_COMPLETION = TRUE
CONFIRM_PROVISIONING = TRUE
SYNCHRONOUS = TRUE

explanation.correct: The WAIT_FOR_COMPLETION parameter on ALTER WAREHOUSE ensures the command waits until all new compute resources are fully provisioned before returning.

distractors.A: VALIDATE_RESOURCES is not a valid ALTER WAREHOUSE parameter.
distractors.C: CONFIRM_PROVISIONING is not a valid parameter.
distractors.D: SYNCHRONOUS is not a valid ALTER WAREHOUSE parameter.

questions.scenario: An Adaptive Warehouse has QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER = 2. The administrator notices significant queuing during peak hours.
questions.stem: What should they do to reduce queuing?

options.text: Decrease MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL to free up resources
Increase QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER to allow more concurrent work
Convert the warehouse back to standard and resize to X-Large
Set QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER to -1

explanation.correct: Increasing QUERY_THROUGHPUT_MULTIPLIER raises the throughput budget, allowing more queries to run concurrently and reducing queuing.

distractors.A: Decreasing MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL limits per-query resources but doesn't directly address throughput/queuing.
distractors.C: Converting back to standard requires manual sizing and loses the adaptive benefits.
distractors.D: -1 is not a valid value; the multiplier is a non-negative integer (0 = unlimited).

questions.scenario: A company creates their first warehouse in a new Snowflake account and wants to understand when credits start being consumed.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about credit consumption timing are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: If some resources fail to provision, credits are only consumed for the successfully provisioned resources
Credits are consumed from the moment the CREATE WAREHOUSE command executes
Credits begin once all compute resources are provisioned for the warehouse
Credits are consumed only when the first query is submitted to the warehouse
Credits begin when the warehouse transitions from RESUMING to STARTED state

explanation.correct: A warehouse begins consuming credits once all compute resources are provisioned. In the rare case when some resources fail to provision, the warehouse only consumes credits for the provisioned resources.

distractors.B: Credits do not start at command execution; they start after resources are provisioned.
distractors.D: Credits are consumed as soon as resources are provisioned, regardless of whether queries have been submitted.
distractors.E: The state transition is not the exact billing trigger; it is the provisioning of resources.

questions.scenario: A Snowflake user initiates a session but no default warehouse is configured at the user level, client configuration file, or connection parameters.
questions.stem: What happens when the user tries to execute a SELECT query?

options.text: The query fails because no warehouse is associated with the session
Snowflake assigns the account's smallest available warehouse automatically
The query runs on the cloud services layer without a warehouse
Snowflake prompts the user to select a warehouse before executing

explanation.correct: Until a session has a warehouse associated with it, queries cannot be submitted. Without any default configured, the query will fail.

distractors.B: Snowflake does not auto-assign a warehouse; the user must specify one.
distractors.C: SELECT queries requiring compute resources cannot run on the cloud services layer alone.
distractors.D: SQL sessions do not have interactive prompts; the query simply fails.

questions.scenario: An interactive warehouse has 10 interactive tables added to it via ALTER WAREHOUSE ADD TABLES. The team wants to add an 11th table.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about the proactive warming limit for interactive warehouses are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Tables beyond the limit cannot be queried at all
The limit applies per cluster, not per warehouse
Tables beyond the limit can still be queried but without proactive cache warming
Proactive warming is limited to 10 interactive tables per warehouse
The limit is permanent and will never be increased

explanation.correct: Tables beyond the 10-table proactive warming limit can still be queried without proactive cache warming, and the limit is 10 interactive tables per warehouse. This is a temporary limitation.

distractors.A: Tables beyond the limit can still be queried; they just don't receive proactive cache warming.
distractors.B: The limit is per warehouse, not per cluster.
distractors.E: This is documented as a temporary limitation that will be increased in the future.

questions.scenario: A team wants to understand the conversion limitations for Adaptive Warehouses.
questions.stem: Which TWO conversions are NOT supported for Adaptive Warehouses? (Select TWO)

options.text: Converting from a standard Medium warehouse to Adaptive
Converting from an X5Large or X6Large warehouse to Adaptive
Converting from a Snowpark-optimized warehouse to Adaptive
Converting from a Gen2 standard Large warehouse to Adaptive
Converting from an X-Large multi-cluster warehouse to Adaptive

explanation.correct: Converting to or from X5Large/X6Large warehouses and converting to or from Snowpark-optimized or interactive warehouses are not supported for Adaptive Warehouses.

distractors.A: Converting a standard Medium warehouse to Adaptive is supported.
distractors.D: Converting a Gen2 standard Large warehouse to Adaptive is supported.
distractors.E: Converting an X-Large multi-cluster warehouse to Adaptive is supported.

questions.scenario: A BI team uses an interactive warehouse with a fallback warehouse configured. A complex query takes 7 seconds on the interactive warehouse.
questions.stem: What happens to this query?

options.text: The query completes on the interactive warehouse after 7 seconds
The query is cancelled after 5 seconds and automatically retried on the fallback warehouse
The query fails with a timeout error returned to the client
The query is split between the interactive and fallback warehouses

explanation.correct: Interactive warehouses have a fixed 5-second statement timeout. With a fallback warehouse configured, queries exceeding this limit are automatically cancelled and retried on the fallback warehouse transparently.

distractors.A: The query cannot run for 7 seconds on an interactive warehouse; the timeout is 5 seconds.
distractors.C: With a fallback warehouse configured, the query is retried rather than returning an error to the client.
distractors.D: Queries are not split; they are retried entirely on the fallback warehouse.

questions.scenario: A company has Adaptive Warehouses for different teams but wants to track per-query costs for their finance Adaptive Warehouse.
questions.stem: Which view provides per-query credit usage for Adaptive Warehouse workloads?

options.text: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY
SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_ACCELERATION_HISTORY
SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_METERING_HISTORY

explanation.correct: QUERY_METERING_HISTORY provides per-query credit usage for Adaptive Warehouse workloads, with latency of up to 1 hour.

distractors.A: WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY provides aggregated warehouse-level credit usage, not per-query detail.
distractors.B: QUERY_HISTORY shows query execution details but not credit costs per query.
distractors.C: QUERY_ACCELERATION_HISTORY shows QAS billing data specifically, not general Adaptive Warehouse per-query costs.

questions.scenario: An administrator is comparing warehouse types to decide which fits their dashboard serving workload requiring sub-second response times at high concurrency.
questions.stem: Which TWO characteristics of interactive warehouses make them suitable for this workload? (Select TWO)

options.text: They use a local storage cache to serve queries with minimal remote reads
They automatically increase warehouse size based on query complexity
They support multi-cluster scaling for high-concurrency workloads
They eliminate the need for table clustering
They can run both standard tables and interactive tables simultaneously

explanation.correct: Interactive warehouses use local storage caching for low-latency reads and support multi-cluster scaling to handle high query concurrency.

distractors.B: Interactive warehouses do not automatically resize; you choose the size based on working set.
distractors.D: Clustering is essential for interactive tables — the CLUSTER BY clause is required at creation.
distractors.E: Interactive warehouses can only query interactive tables; standard tables require a standard warehouse.

questions.scenario: A team creates a warehouse that starts in 'Suspended' state. They then execute ALTER WAREHOUSE my_wh RESUME.
questions.stem: What is the minimum period the warehouse will be billed for once it resumes?

options.text: 60 seconds
1 second
30 seconds
300 seconds

explanation.correct: Credits are billed per-second with a 60-second (1-minute) minimum each time the warehouse is resumed.

distractors.B: Per-second billing applies after the first 60 seconds; 1 second is below the minimum.
distractors.C: 30 seconds is below the minimum billing period of 60 seconds.
distractors.D: 300 seconds (5 minutes) is not the minimum billing period.

questions.scenario: A newly created Adaptive Warehouse has not yet run any queries.
questions.stem: How much has the account been charged for this warehouse so far?

options.text: A minimum 1-hour charge for creating the warehouse
Nothing; charges start when the first query runs
A one-time creation fee based on MAX_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_LEVEL
Per-second charges from the moment of creation

explanation.correct: You are not charged for creating an Adaptive Warehouse; charges start when the first query runs.

distractors.A: There is no minimum 1-hour charge for creation; billing is query-based.
distractors.C: There is no one-time creation fee for Adaptive Warehouses.
distractors.D: Per-second charges do not start until queries are executed.

questions.stem: Which THREE query statuses are shown in the warehouse load monitoring bar chart? (Select THREE)

options.text: Running
Compiling
Blocked
Queued (Provisioning)
Cancelled
Optimizing

explanation.correct: The warehouse load monitoring chart shows Running, Queued (Provisioning), Blocked, and Queued statuses. Three of these four are listed among the options.

distractors.B: Compiling is not a separate status shown in the load monitoring chart.
distractors.E: Cancelled queries are not displayed as a status in the load chart.
distractors.F: Optimizing is not a query status shown in the load monitoring chart.

questions.scenario: An organization uses Adaptive Warehouses. For Adaptive Warehouses, QAS usage appears different in billing compared to standard warehouses.
questions.stem: How is QAS usage reported for Adaptive Warehouses?

options.text: As a separate line item in the QUERY_ACCELERATION_HISTORY view
Included in compute credits and not shown as a separate credit column
Billed at double the rate of standard warehouse QAS
QAS is not available for Adaptive Warehouses

explanation.correct: For Adaptive Warehouses, QAS usage is included in compute credits and does not appear as a separate credit column.

distractors.A: QUERY_ACCELERATION_HISTORY applies to standard warehouses where QAS is billed separately.
distractors.C: There is no documented double-rate billing for Adaptive Warehouse QAS.
distractors.D: QAS functionality is included in Adaptive Warehouses; it is managed automatically.
